title: Signal Weigher: lightweight attribution layer for per-route/model/customer cost & latency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a small, pluggable attribution component (Signal Weigher) that runs in the analytics pipeline to produce deterministic, explainable per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency contributions. The service should emit a compact signature and attribution vector for each request slice that other downstream aggregators can consume for chargeback, dashboards, and anomaly detection. Focus is on low-latency enrichment, backfill-friendly semantics, and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Service emits attribution vector (route, model_variant, tenant, token_buckets) in <50ms per event in pipeline tests
Vectors are stable across replays (idempotent for same telemetry + config) and include provenance metadata (schema version, algorithm id)
Matches ground-truth within 1.5% avg error vs batch reconciler on synthetic workload for cost allocation
Provides an opt-in detailed breakdown mode for debug tenants guarded by RBAC and audit logs
Integration tests with billing rollup pipeline pass and dashboards surface new fields without schema conflicts
progress_updates: 2025-01-20: Spike completed — evaluated three approaches: single-pass proportional splitter, causal-span-based apportioner, and hybrid time-window smoothing. Hybrid chosen for best tradeoff between accuracy and perf.

2025-01-28: Prototype implemented in Rust microservice behind a Kafka topic; emits JSON vector and a compact base64 signature. Microbenchmarks: median 28ms/event on c5.xlarge-equivalent; tail 95th 72ms — needs improvements.
2025-02-06: Worked with infra to add CPU pinning and batch coalescing; tail improved to 40ms. Added deterministic sort key to ensure replay idempotency.
2025-02-12: Design review with PM & Console team. Decided to expose two modes: lightweight (top-3 contributors) and debug (full vector). PM requested tenant opt-in flag at route level.
2025-02-18: Security kick-off scheduled; draft threat model written. Data flows annotated for PII and billing-critical tags. KMS integration required for signing keys.
design_feedback: PM (Lena Fischer) requested explicit handling for model-variant fallbacks so attribution doesn't double-count when runtime routes to a cheaper variant.
Console UX (Ravi Shah) suggested adding a derived field `primary_cost_driver` to simplify charting in dashboards.
SRE (Anita Gomez) emphasized adding health-check metrics and circuit-breaker for when upstream telemetry lags >2 minutes.
implementation_notes: Implementation will be a small service (Weigher) implemented in Rust with a protobuf envelope. It subscribes to enriched telemetry topic, enriches records with attribution vector, and republishes to `telemetry.attribution.v1`.

Use a two-pass algorithm: 1) fast proportional apportion by token counts and model FLOPs estimate, 2) correction pass using causal-span overlap when spans are present to reassign micro-latency fractions.
Persistence: keep only ephemeral state. For backfills, provide a deterministic replay mode that accepts a `replay_id` and produces identical vectors for same input and config.

Schema: follow console-telemetry v3; new fields names: attribution_vector_v1 (compact base64), attribution_summary (top-3), attribution_provenance (algorithm_id, schema_version). Add unit tests for schema evolution.
Telemetry metrics to emit: weigher_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), vector_size_bytes, backfill_replay_count, failed_signature_verifications.
rollout_plan: alpha: run as consumer-only in staging for 2 weeks; sample 1% of traffic for debug tenants
beta: enable lightweight mode for 25% of production tenant traffic; monitor cost deltas and p95 latency
GA: default lightweight enabled, debug mode opt-in per-tenant via Console toggle
metrics: Fraction of requests with complete span data
risks: Double-counting when runtime model fallback occurs — mitigated by routing provenance and de-dup keys
Performance regression in pipeline causing increased end-to-end latency — mitigated via batching, CPU pinning, and circuit-breaker
Schema churn causing dashboard breakage — mitigated by schema versioning and feature-gated rollout
Security: exposure of billing attribution for tenants — mitigated by RBAC gating and KMS-signed vectors
test_plan: Unit tests for algorithm determinism, fuzz tests with synthetic telemetry (varied token lengths, multi-tenant spikes), integration tests with billing rollup in staging, and a 1-week shadow run comparing produced vectors to the batch reconciler. Include a chaos test where spans are delayed or lost to validate graceful degradation.
